title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a space (analytic or topological, ultimately the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν} with its boundary stratification) with a stratification by strata X_i. Because boundary divisors can self-intersect, Grothendieck works with LOCAL data: germs at x of closures of strata (local branches), not global strata.

Previous page: a 'strict' r-flag at x is (x, Σ_x) with Σ_x a chain of germs at x, \bar X_{i_0} ⊂ \bar X_{i_1} ⊂ … ⊂ \bar X_{i_r}, where x lies in the open stratum X_{i_0}. The space of such flags, D*_{Δ_r}, with the obvious topology, has a forgetful map D*_{Δ_r} → X (301). This map is a local immersion. For a normal crossings divisor, D*_{Δ_r} recovers the coverings (disjoint unions over flags of index sets) of the earlier sections.

Problem on this page: one wants face maps D*_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_{r'}} for injections Δ_{r'} → Δ_r. Strict flags are not stable under faces. Deleting the smallest member \bar X_{i_0} leaves a chain whose bottom stratum X_{i_1} contains x only in its closure, not in its interior. Hence a substitute for D_{Δ_{r'}} is needed.

Fix: define non-strict ('positifs, pas stricts') flags (x, Σ_x), requiring only x ∈ \bar X_{i_0}. Use the same germ topology. This gives spaces D_{Δ_r} and maps D_{Δ_r} → X (302), still local immersions. The strict-flag space D°_{Δ_r} is a canonical open subspace of D_{Δ_r}. Now the D_{Δ_r} form a semi-simplicial ('½ simplicial') space; the maps he calls dégénérescence are presumably the face maps.

The page ends by asking whether this semi-simplicial space is the nerve of a category in (Top). The next page answers via the Segal map D_{Δ_2} → D_{Δ_1} ×_{D_{Δ_0}} D_{Δ_1}, which is a homeomorphism because containment of germs is transitive. The result is a topological category attached to any local stratification:
- objects: D_{Δ_0}, pairs (point, germ of a local stratum closure through it);
- arrows: D_{Δ_1}, local incidences \bar X_{i_0} ⊂ \bar X_{i_1} at x;
- source, target and composition: the obvious ones.

Purpose: to encode the combinatorial-topological 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν} (incidences of boundary strata, including self-intersections) as a simplicial/categorical object over X. This is a step toward the dévissage of stratified structures and the Teichmüller tower gluing data of Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No real mathematical error. Note that D_{Δ_r} → X is a local immersion (locally a homeomorphism onto a locally closed piece, the branch \bar X_{i_0} near x), not a local homeomorphism onto X. It is implicitly assumed that germs of stratum closures at nearby points y are canonically induced (local branches spread out). This needs a mild regularity hypothesis such as local finiteness or local conic structure of the stratification; it is fine for normal crossings and for the Deligne–Mumford boundary.

Terminology: with only injective Δ_{r'} → Δ_r one gets face maps, so 'morphismes de dégénérescence' should be read as faces unless repetitions are allowed in non-strict flags. In that case the object would be fully simplicial, not merely ½-simplicial.

ideas.what: Semi-simplicial space of local flags of germs of stratum closures, with non-strict flags introduced so that face maps exist; strict flags form an open subspace
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial (local) resolution of a normal crossings / stratified space; local version of the Deligne semi-simplicial space of normalized intersections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II/III, 1971–74) for normal crossings divisors; general stratified versions in later work on stratified spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures) is close in spirit, but this explicit construction is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Topological category attached to a local stratification: objects = germs of local strata at points, arrows = local incidences, Segal condition D_2 ≅ D_1 ×_{D_0} D_1
ideas.modern_name: Étale topological category / poset of local strata; discrete model of the exit-path category of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, early 1990s), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Working with germs of local branches to handle self-intersecting boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: Local strata / branches; stratification by stable graphs with automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; cf. Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen; later Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne (boundary complex as generalized cone complex)

missed.claim: Grothendieck packages the local incidence structure of an arbitrary stratification into a topological category (an étale-type category over X) whose nerve is the space of non-strict flags of local strata germs. This is a point-set, germ-level precursor of the exit-path category of a stratified space. It is aimed at the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}, where it would encode the incidence of stable-graph strata including self-intersections, i.e. the data later used for the boundary complex and tropical moduli.
missed.quote: Cette fois-ci on a fait ce qu'il fallait pour que les D_{Δ_r} forment un système ½ simplicial d'espaces
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an alternative, purely topological model of the stratified homotopy type and of the gluing data at infinity of moduli spaces of curves. It sits between exit-path ∞-categories (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) and generalized cone complexes / boundary complexes of M̄_{g,n} (Abramovich–Caporaso–Payne, Chan–Galatius–Payne). It is of historical interest as a likely 1980s anticipation, though the idea is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, natural construction (semi-simplicial space of non-strict local flags satisfying the Segal condition, hence a topological category of local strata) anticipating exit-path-category ideas in a germ-theoretic form. However, it is fairly routine once the problem is posed, and analogous objects (Deligne's semi-simplicial resolutions, exit-path categories) are well established.

Last line is uncertain. It likely begins a question continuing on the next page, '... ½ simplicial sont-ils [le nerf d'] une catégorie dans (Top) ?', rather than 'Les ½ simplicial ont-ils'.
